name: q-key-opens-the-quality-popover-and-escape-closes-it
description: The quality-and-speed popover is reachable and dismissible from the keyboard alone: Q opens it and Escape closes it again. No pointer is involved at either end, and Escape dismisses the overlay rather than the player.

steps.note: The key is delivered to whatever holds focus, so the window is given it first - the way clicking the title bar or arriving from the page would. This is the real precondition for the shortcut rather than a formality.
PlayerDialog::onShellKey maps Q to shell_->openSettings() (PlayerDialog.cpp:2918-2919), so the shell's own gear handler runs with no pointer involved.

steps.name: widgetVisible
steps.note: The visible proof that Q opened it. The popover is hidden at construction (ShellWidgets.cpp:146) and only shown by popupNear() (ShellWidgets.cpp:306-307), so this step fails the run on any build where Q did not reach openSettings(). A manifest cannot assert 'visible: true' mid-run - every assertion is decided after the last step - so this gate carries the open state and the assertion below carries the closed one.

popupNear() gave the overlay the focus (ShellWidgets.cpp:327), so Escape lands in SettingsFlyout::keyPressEvent, which closes it (ShellWidgets.cpp:330-336). PlayerShell::dismissOverlay() reaches the same overlay from the shell's own handler (PlayerShell.cpp:1310-1312); either route closes the popover and neither closes the window.

assertions.note: Escape closed the popover. Visible - not merely present - because the widget is built either way: hide() runs in its constructor (ShellWidgets.cpp:146) and popupNear() shows it again, so an existence check would pass on a build where the key never arrived.

The quality half went with it. qualitySection_ is shown by setQualityOptions() (ShellWidgets.cpp:284) and its isVisible() is false again as soon as its parent is hidden, so this fails if the overlay was torn down without taking its children - a leaked popover that still computes visible for its own rows.

The discriminating check, and the reason this manifest is not just 'a key was pressed'. Both the flyout's own handler (ShellWidgets.cpp:332) and PlayerShell's (PlayerShell.cpp:1310) claim Escape for the overlay before anything else sees it; had the overlay refused it, onShellKey would have gone on to close() (PlayerDialog.cpp:2906). So a build that dismissed the window instead of the popover passes the two assertions above and fails here.
And the core never stopped. Read from mpv itself rather than from the Qt cache written alongside it, so a build that muted the overlay by pausing fails here instead of passing as a clean dismiss.
